title: Correlation vs Test Frequency Sweep
description: A Chart.js line sweep of correlation magnitude against test frequency, showing a sharp peak at the captured signal's frequency and near-zero response elsewhere.
creator: Real-Time DSP on a $5 Microcontroller
author: Dan McCreary
subject: Digital Signal Processing
Correlation
Frequency Analysis

learningObjectives: Examine correlation magnitude across a swept test frequency
Distinguish the true-frequency peak from near-zero off-peak response
Relate peak width to window length

controls.label: Any point on the line
controls.purpose: Tooltip with exact test frequency and correlation

equations: I = sum x[n] sin(2 pi f n / fs)
Q = sum x[n] cos(2 pi f n / fs)
assumptions: A single unit-amplitude sinusoid with no noise
Rectangular window of 256 samples at 8 kHz
limitations: Sidelobes and scalloping loss shown here are genuine consequences of the rectangular window; windowing to reduce them is covered in Chapter 15

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Swept-parameter response curve with a marked ground truth
keyQuestions: How large is the peak compared with a typical off-peak value?
What sets the width of the peak?
commonMisconceptions: That off-peak correlation is exactly zero at every frequency
That the peak always reaches exactly 1.0
assessmentOpportunities: Predict the effect of shortening the window to 64 samples
